ballot: Democrats hold 254 seats to Republicans' 166, with 15 races still undecided, going into the 120th Congress (ABC News, Nov. 10, 2026)
senate: Democrats reach 55 seats after Scott Colom's win in Mississippi; in Alaska, Mary Peltola leads Dan Sullivan 49.9% to 46% with about 97% counted, and ranked-choice tabulation is due on Nov. 18 (Yahoo News/AP, Nov. 11; Alaska Public Media, Nov. 13–14)
approval: 32% approve, 65% disapprove in Reuters/Ipsos (Nov. 6–9); 32% approve in Economist/YouGov (Nov. 9–11); the New York Times average is 36% approve, 61% disapprove (Yahoo News, Nov. 2026)
ledger_source: ABC News, Yahoo News/AP, Alaska Public Media, Al Jazeera and Yahoo News poll round-up, Nov. 6–14, 2026

headlines.headline: Colom defeats Hyde-Smith in Mississippi
headlines.short: Colom wins Mississippi, the first Democratic senator there since 1989.
headlines.summary: Democrat Scott Colom beat Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith 49.2% to 48.7%, a race separated by 65 votes on election night; Hyde-Smith conceded on Nov. 11. Colom is Mississippi's first Democratic senator since 1989 and the first Black candidate elected to the Senate from the state in more than 140 years. Democrats now hold 55 Senate seats.

headlines.headline: Peltola nears 50% as Alaska's count winds down
headlines.short: Alaska: Peltola leads Sullivan 49.9% to 46%; ranked-choice count Nov. 18.
headlines.summary: With about 97% of the vote counted, Democrat Mary Peltola has 49.9% to Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan's 46%. Just short of a first-choice majority, the race is likely to go to ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18, after the deadline for overseas ballots. The Associated Press has not called it.

headlines.headline: Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as chief of staff
headlines.short: Miller replaces Wiles as White House chief of staff after the midterm losses.
headlines.summary: Trump named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff on Nov. 6, after Susie Wiles resigned; she moves to the Trump Political Operation. Miller, architect of the immigration crackdown, is seen as signalling a harder line for Trump's final two years. Incoming Oversight chair Robert Garcia said Democrats will keep investigating Miller.

headlines.headline: Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader
headlines.short: Jordan beats Scalise 106–73 to lead House Republicans in the minority.
headlines.summary: House Republicans chose Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, 106 votes to 73 over Majority Leader Steve Scalise, after Speaker Mike Johnson said he would not run. Tom Emmer becomes minority whip. In the Senate, John Thune was re-elected Republican leader.

headlines.headline: House sidelines Hegseth impeachment
headlines.short: House votes 211–204 to send Hegseth impeachment to committee.
headlines.summary: Republican Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, over the Iran war and strikes on alleged drug boats, were referred to the Judiciary Committee by 211 votes to 204, effectively blocking a direct vote. Democrats could revive the effort when they take the House in January.

podcasts.summary: "Susie Wiles Out, Stephen Miller In: What is Trump Thinking?" (Nov 9) — Katty Kay and Anthony Scaramucci on Miller's first moves as chief of staff, Trump's first interview after the midterms, and what Democrats should prioritise in Congress.
"Is this the end of the Trump era?" (Nov 6) — The Economist's US team asks whether the midterms end a decade of Trump's dominance, and how Democrats might use their new power.

wildcard: Gavin Newsom says he'll decide on a 2028 run "at the beginning of the year" — telling Turkey's Anadolu news agency at the UN climate summit in Antalya.
